entries.declaredBehavior: A leading tab indents like four spaces for code-block and list detection.
entries.boundary: Tab-stop expansion inside content is approximate; some interior-tab cases diverge from the reference.

entries.declaredBehavior: A backslash before an ASCII punctuation character emits that character literally rather than as Markdown syntax.
entries.boundary: A backslash before a non-punctuation character is left literal; escapes do not apply inside code spans or math.

entries.declaredBehavior: Named and numeric HTML entities are preserved verbatim so the browser resolves them.
entries.boundary: Entities are not decoded to their target character during rendering, so some reference outputs that substitute the character diverge.

entries.declaredBehavior: Block structure is resolved before inline structure, matching CommonMark precedence.
entries.boundary: n/a

entries.declaredBehavior: A line of three or more `-`, `*`, or `_` (optionally spaced) becomes `<hr>`.
entries.boundary: Some inline-vs-rule ambiguities (e.g. emphasis runs) diverge at the edges.

entries.declaredBehavior: `#`–`######` followed by a space become `<h1>`–`<h6>` with an auto-generated slug `id`; trailing `#` are stripped.
entries.boundary: More than six `#`, or no space after the `#` run, is not a heading and falls back to a paragraph.

entries.declaredBehavior: A paragraph line underlined by `=` or `-` becomes `<h1>`/`<h2>`.
entries.boundary: Multi-line setext content and some interaction with lists/indentation diverge at the edges.

entries.declaredBehavior: Lines indented four spaces (or a tab) become `<pre><code>` with the indentation stripped.
entries.boundary: The trailing newline inside the code element is not always emitted, so output can diverge by a final `\n`.

entries.declaredBehavior: ``` ``` ``` and `~~~` fences become `<pre><code>`; an info string becomes `class="language-…"` and drives syntax highlighting.
entries.boundary: An unterminated fence renders to end of document; the trailing newline inside the code element can diverge from the reference.

entries.declaredBehavior: Block-level raw HTML passthrough is not implemented; such input is treated as ordinary Markdown text and escaped where unsafe.
entries.boundary: Authored angle-bracket text is preserved (escaped); no block-level HTML is emitted verbatim.

entries.declaredBehavior: Reference-style link definitions (`[id]: url`) and reference links (`[text][id]`) are not resolved.
entries.boundary: Definition lines render as literal paragraph text rather than being consumed; inline links (`[text](url)`) are unaffected.

entries.declaredBehavior:
Runs of non-blank lines become `

`; a blank line separates paragraphs.
entries.boundary:
Soft line breaks within a paragraph render as `
` (intentional, editor-style), where the reference joins with a newline.

entries.declaredBehavior: Blank lines separate blocks and are otherwise ignored.
entries.boundary: n/a

entries.declaredBehavior: `>`-prefixed lines become `<blockquote>` with their content re-rendered as Markdown.
entries.boundary:
Soft line breaks inside a quote render as `
` (intentional); lazy-continuation edge cases diverge.

entries.declaredBehavior: `-`/`*`/`+` and `N.`/`N)` markers become `<li>`; indentation drives nesting.
entries.boundary: Loose/tight detection, multi-paragraph items, and some indentation edges diverge from the reference.

entries.declaredBehavior: Consecutive items of one kind become a single `<ul>`/`<ol>`; `<ol>` honours the first start number.
entries.boundary: List-tightness and marker-change splitting follow simplified rules that diverge at the edges.

entries.declaredBehavior: Inline parsing runs in a fixed precedence: code spans, then escapes, math, entities, autolinks, raw HTML, then emphasis/links/images.
entries.boundary: n/a

entries.declaredBehavior: Backtick runs become `<code>` with the content HTML-escaped; the longest matching run delimits the span.
entries.boundary: Some backtick-balancing and surrounding-space-trim edges diverge from the reference.

entries.declaredBehavior: `*`/`_` produce `<em>`, doubled produce `<strong>`, triple produce nested strong-emphasis; `~~` produces `<del>`.
entries.boundary: Complex flanking/nesting cases from the CommonMark emphasis algorithm are simplified and diverge at the edges.

entries.declaredBehavior: `[text](url "title")` becomes `<a href>` with optional `title`; dangerous schemes are neutralised.
entries.boundary: Only inline links are resolved (no reference links); nested-bracket and title-edge cases diverge.

entries.declaredBehavior: `![alt](src "title")` becomes ``, with optional Pandoc-style size attributes.
entries.boundary: Only inline image syntax is resolved; reference-style images and some alt-text edges diverge.

entries.declaredBehavior: `<scheme:...>` and `<email>` angle-bracket autolinks become `<a href>`.
entries.boundary: Some scheme-validation and edge cases diverge; bare-text autolinking is the GFM extension (separate entry).

entries.declaredBehavior: A safe subset of inline HTML tags passes through; unsafe tags (e.g. `<script>`) are HTML-escaped.
entries.boundary: The allowed-tag set is narrower than CommonMark, so disallowed/unknown tags are escaped rather than passed through.

entries.declaredBehavior:
A line ending in two spaces or a backslash becomes `
`.
entries.boundary:
Because soft breaks also render as `
`, hard and soft breaks converge on `
` (intentional editor behaviour).

entries.declaredBehavior:
A soft line break renders as `
` so each authored line stays on its own line.
entries.boundary: Intentional divergence from the reference, which renders a soft break as a newline/space.

entries.declaredBehavior: Plain text is emitted with HTML-significant characters escaped.
entries.boundary: n/a

entries.declaredBehavior: Pipe tables become `<table>` with `<thead>`/`<tbody>`; column alignment is emitted as `style="text-align:…"`.
entries.boundary: Alignment uses CSS `style` rather than the GFM `align` attribute (intentional); a delimiter row without leading/trailing pipes is not recognised and falls back to a paragraph.

entries.declaredBehavior: `- [ ]`/`- [x]` items become `<li>` with a `<input type=checkbox>`; the list carries `class="task-list"`.
entries.boundary: Checkboxes are left enabled (not `disabled`) and carry `data-md2-task-line` so a preview click can toggle them — intentional divergence from the reference.

entries.declaredBehavior: `~~text~~` becomes `<del>text</del>`.
entries.boundary: n/a

entries.declaredBehavior: Bare-text autolinking (`www.`/`http(s)`/email without angle brackets) is not implemented.
entries.boundary: Such text renders literally; use angle-bracket autolinks or explicit links instead.

entries.declaredBehavior: Unsafe HTML tags are HTML-escaped, which is at least as strict as GFM's disallowed-raw-HTML filtering.
entries.boundary: Markdown2 escapes a broader set than GFM filters, so output diverges while remaining safe.

entries.declaredBehavior: A leading `---` fenced YAML block is parsed as front matter.
entries.boundary: Only a document-leading block is treated as front matter; malformed YAML degrades to visible text.

entries.declaredBehavior: `[TOC]` expands to a nested table of contents generated from the document headings.
entries.boundary: With no headings, `[TOC]` produces an empty list rather than failing.

entries.declaredBehavior: Inline `$…$` and display `$$…$$` TeX are typeset offline with bundled KaTeX (incl. mhchem).
entries.boundary: Commands outside KaTeX's subset render as an inline KaTeX error rather than blanking; currency `$` and `$` in code stay literal.

entries.declaredBehavior: `mermaid`, `flow`, and `sequence` fenced blocks render offline with bundled engines in the Read-mode preview.
entries.boundary: Invalid diagram source falls back to showing its raw text instead of blanking the preview.

entries.declaredBehavior: `[^id]` references and `[^id]:` definitions become numbered superscript links plus a footnotes section with back-references.
entries.boundary: An undefined reference renders as literal text; definitions are collected regardless of position.

entries.declaredBehavior: Pandoc-style `{width=… height=…}` after an image sets its dimensions.
entries.boundary: Invalid attributes are ignored and the image still renders.

entries.declaredBehavior: Pasted/dropped images are saved into a configurable document-relative folder and linked in place.
entries.boundary: A missing local image shows an explicit broken-image placeholder rather than a blank.
